transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Time: 16:00 UTC (60 minutes)
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Nina Alvarez (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood CSM), Samir Patel (Vectora Head of MLOps), Lina Zhou (Vectora SRE), Marta Ruiz (Product), Devon Gray (Finance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
Vectora has seen two short but high-concurrency spikes in the last 30 days causing tail latency above SLO on a handful of endpoints. Team is concerned about upcoming Q3 rollout which adds heavier context windows. Redwood proposed a short capacity/risk sprint: run an extended stress test on Dedicated nodes with persistent KV caching, measure tail latency, and then decide on reserved commit + burst policy. Pricing scenario and pilot review scheduled.

-- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) --
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um, quick roll call and we'll, yeah, jump into the pulse. Marcus, do you want to kick off?
[00:18] Marcus: yeah thanks, Jordan. Hello Vectora folks. Today's goal is to align on the capacity risk sprint, confirm metrics we care about, and set action owners.
[00:28] Samir: yep, thanks. We had two spikes last month where our chat endpoints saw a 3x concurrency increase for 15 to 40 minutes. Latency crept up and we hit our 99.9 P95.. P99.9? yeah, that's what I mean, and that tripped some backend timeouts.
[00:46] Lina: and to add we saw KV cache misses on long contexts, so the K-V, uh, prefix cache wasn't warming fast enough when a lot of users hit similar flows.
[00:56] Nina: okay, that makes sense. When you say long contexts, are we talking 4K tokens or more?
[01:04] Samir: mostly 8k for the new model test, some 16k in a few reseller flows. We didn't fully anticipate the combinatorial growth.
[01:12] Jordan: right. So the emergent problem is sequence length distribution changed after the feature toggle last week, plus the bursty traffic pattern. That raises both latency and per-token cost.
[01:24] Marta: finance is worried, too — Devon, you saw the bill bump for the last spike?
[01:29] Devon: yep, the cost in July spiked ~28% against baseline for inference spend. We need to understand commit options vs on-demand. If we reserve too much, we pay for idle. If we don't, spikes kill UX.
[01:41] Jordan: that's exactly the tradeoff. So our proposed approach: 1) run a 24h stress-run on a Dedicated pool with persistent KV and real traffic replay; 2) measure tail percentiles P95-P99.99, cold/warm start deltas, and token e2e cost; 3) evaluate reserve + burst pricing vs hosted scaling; 4) decide a commit level for Q3 rollout.
[02:04] Samir: does dedicated give us isolation for the audit folks? I mean, for SOC2 and SSO integration?
[02:11] Nina: Dedicated is isolated GPU pools; for Private we do a private control plane. For SOC2 the audit logs and KMS integrations are available. Sorry sometimes the transcript says "Red wood dedicate" in the docs, but that's the same product.
[02:24] Lina: and to be clear we need SAML SSO for admin console and RBAC mapping for teams.
[02:30] Jordan: yep we'll include the SSO/RBAC checks in the risk sprint.
[02:35] Marcus: quick question on model variants — if latency is bad on the LLM with 16k context, can we fall back to a quantized variant or lower-precision instance? What's the degradation pattern?
[02:46] Nina: yes, we can route by policy. The runtime supports model variants: a quantized v1, and a full fp16 variant. Fallbacks are possible but you need to test quality regression. We'll surface the tradeoffs — sometimes top-K behavior changes slightly.
[02:59] Samir: okay will need to verify quality for our test prompts.
[03:05] Marta: and timeline — we want the Q3 rollout in three weeks, that's tight. What's realistic?
[03:12] Jordan: if we run the sprint this week and get results by next Tuesday, we can decide commit level and have ops run a dry-run. It's tight but doable if owners move fast.
[03:21] Marcus: can we capture what metrics matter? I'll list: P50/P95/P99/P99.9 latencies, tail token cost, error rates (429/500), cache hit ratio, and autoscale stabilization time. Anything else?
[03:34] Lina: also memory evictions on KV store and per-host GPU memory pressure.
[03:38] Nina: and cold-start delta — first request after scale-up.
[03:41] Devon: finance wants a cost-per-1000-requests scenario too, and a worst-case monthly burn if spikes repeat.
[03:48] Jordan: noted.

[10:12] Speaker 3: (mumbling) so the replay workload, do you have traces or just synthetic?
[10:19] Samir: we can provide 7 days of anonymized traces for replay; they reflect the real mix (chat, embeddings, rerank). Some fields will be redacted.
[10:27] Nina: perfect, that helps for realistic KV-access patterns.
[10:31] Marcus: ok, action: Samir will upload traces to the secure bucket and give SE the link.

[14:02] Jordan: about pricing — we have three knobs: reserved commit, burst credits, and autoscale headroom. Reserved gives predictable unit economics but costs fixed fee; burst lets you scale above commit for short windows. We'll prepare 3 example scenarios.
[14:18] Devon: can you show cost delta for 30% spike for 1 hour vs sustained 8-hour spike? That's what finance cares about.
[14:27] Jordan: yes. Nina, you'll help with the throughput assumptions?
[14:31] Nina: yup. I'll pair with Jordan on the scenarios. We'll include token cost and infra overhead.

[23:45] Lina: a security question — please confirm KMS + HSM support for private keys and audit trail retention options. We have compliance review on Aug 6.
[23:55] Nina: yes KMS integrations supported (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM on private deployments; audit logs can be set to 90/365 day retention per policy. We'll share the security pack and the SOC2 cert link.
[24:10] Jordan: I'll attach the security packet to the follow-up email.

[30:00] Marta: small nit: when we did the PoC we observed slightly different tokenization with the quantized model, some outputs had odd spans. We need to run evals on our prompt set.
[30:12] Nina: good point — we'll run the prompt set with the fallback variant and produce an automatic eval diff report.

[36:05] Jordan: okay, recap and owners: Nina runs 24h stress on Dedicated with persistent KV and reports P95-P99.99 and cache hit rates; Samir uploads 7-day traces; Jordan produces pricing scenarios for commit+burst; Marcus defines exact metric thresholds for go/no-go; Marcus and Marcus? sorry, Marcus and Jordan will do a short ops runbook.
[36:32] Samir: timeline: upload traces by 2026-07-23, run by 2026-07-26, results and decision by 2026-07-28.
[36:40] Devon: finance will review the pricing doc and give feedback by 2026-07-25.

[45:10] Nina: quick tech aside — when we do the replay, please include header flags to simulate user identity; we want to check per-tenant caching behavior. If all traffic looks identical caching will be too optimistic.
[45:24] Samir: good call, we'll include tenant IDs.

[50:00] Jordan: any blockers?
[50:03] Lina: none from SRE, but need the secure bucket link and an itemized list of endpoints to target.
[50:09] Jordan: Samir will provide.

[55:15] Marta: thanks everyone. Please send the notes and timeline.
[55:20] Jordan: will do. Nina, Marcus — we sync after the run.
[55:25] Marcus: thanks all.
[55:30] Samir: thanks.
[55:34] Devon: bye.

End of transcript.

Post-call notes: Redwood to attach benchmark template, security packet (SOC2, KMS/HSM details), and pricing scenarios. CSM to create calendar invite for 2026-07-29 pilot-review.
